sections.h2: How does property tax work in Shelby County, Alabama?
sections.html:
A Shelby County owner pays property tax on an assessed value multiplied by the millage rates of the taxing bodies that cover the parcel. The Alabama Department of Revenue explains a mill as one tenth of one cent and gives a worked example: a $100,000 appraised value at a 10 percent assessment rate becomes a $10,000 assessed value, which at a county rate of 0.0325 produces a $325 bill.

That example uses the state's own illustration, not a Shelby County rate. Your actual bill depends on the millage for your city, school district and any special districts, which the county tax office can give you for your parcel. We could not open a Shelby County page listing current rates, so none are quoted here.

Two things can raise a bill. A taxing authority can raise the millage, or the appraised value can rise through a court-ordered reappraisal or a market increase. The department's FAQ says all Alabama counties now run annual reappraisal, reviewing one quarter of the county each year, so every parcel is looked at over a four-year cycle.

sections.h2: What are the key tax dates for a Shelby County house?
sections.html:
Alabama taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31. If they go unpaid, the department's timetable runs from delinquency on January 1 to a turnover to the probate court in February, a court meeting in March, advertising in April and a tax sale in May.

WhenWhat happens
October 1Taxes due
December 31Last day before delinquency; deadline to report improvements made by October 1
January 1Taxes delinquent
FebruaryTurned over to probate court
MarchProbate court meets
AprilAdvertised for sale
MayTax sale

Counties are not required to mail notices. The Revenue Department says the tax bill is a courtesy, and you owe the tax whether or not one arrives.

sections.h2: What changes to a house have to be reported in Shelby County?
sections.html:
Owners must visit the county revenue office by December 31 and sign a new assessment for any improvement or removal made on or before October 1 of that year. The list of reportable items includes new structures and additions, pools, remodeling, an added bath or fireplace, a patio, deck, carport or garage.

Normal upkeep does not count. Re-roofing, minor repairs and painting do not require a reassessment. If you are preparing a Shelby County house for sale, keep a record of any work that fits the first list, because an unreported addition can surface later as a corrected assessment.

  • Reportable: additions, pools, decks, garages, carports, added baths
  • Not reportable: re-roofing, painting, minor repairs
  • Deadline: December 31 for work done by October 1

sections.h2: Does Shelby County offer a homestead exemption?
sections.html:
Yes. Alabama defines a homestead as a single-family, owner-occupied dwelling and its land, up to 160 acres, occupied as the primary residence on the first day of the tax year. Owners over 65, permanently and totally disabled owners, and blind owners are exempt from the state portion, though county taxes may still be due.

You claim an exemption at the local county office. The state page does not list Shelby's own exemption amounts, so ask the county for them. The state ties the exemption to the owner who occupies the home on the first day of the tax year, so a buyer who moves in applies for their own.

sections.h2: What do you do about property tax when you buy or sell in Shelby County?
sections.html:
The state's guidance for a purchase is short: record the deed in the probate office, then assess the property at the county revenue office, and bring the deed. Make sure any taxes for the year are paid, and know that the bill may still carry the previous owner's name. The new owner is responsible for the taxes on property they own whatever name is on the bill.

For a seller, that means the closing statement should say who pays the current year's tax. Tax proration practice is a matter for the contract and the title company, and we did not find a Shelby County rule on it, so settle it in writing. Report any address change to the county office in writing as well.

Appeals follow their own deadlines, and we could not confirm the Shelby County appeal window from an official page. If you think an assessment is wrong, ask the county office how to file and by what date before you list the house.

sections.h2: What if Shelby County taxes are unpaid when I want to sell?
sections.html:
You can still sell, but the timetable keeps running. A bill that is not paid by December 31 turns delinquent on January 1 and moves toward the probate court and a possible May tax sale, so the earlier you find an unpaid balance, the more choices you have.

If a balance is due at closing, the contract and the closing agent can provide for paying it out of the sale proceeds. A sale to a cash buyer can close on a short schedule, which helps when a deadline is close, though we do not promise a closing date before we have seen the title.

  • Ask the county tax office for the payoff on every year that shows a balance.
  • Check whether any improvement was left unreported.
  • Keep proof of any exemption you held in case the office asks.

sections.h2: Where is Shelby County and what are its towns?
sections.html:
Shelby County is in central Alabama, covers 810 square miles and has Columbiana as its seat, according to Wikipedia's county entry. Alabaster is the largest city, and the county had 223,024 residents in 2020 with a 2025 estimate of 238,552.

The county's incorporated places include Alabaster, Calera, Chelsea, Columbiana, Helena, Montevallo, Pelham, Westover, Harpersville, Indian Springs Village, Wilsonville and Wilton. Birmingham, Hoover, Leeds, Vestavia Hills and Vincent have parts inside the county but extend into neighboring ones, so confirm which county's records cover your parcel.

Interstate 65 and U.S. 31 run north to south, and U.S. 231 and U.S. 280 cross the east. Commercial flights use Birmingham-Shuttlesworth International Airport in neighboring Jefferson County, while the Shelby County Airport handles general aviation.

sections.h2: What do Shelby County property owners like to know about the area?
sections.html:
The county has several parks and sites that buyers recognize. Wikipedia lists Oak Mountain State Park, Oak Mountain Amphitheatre, Cahaba River Wildlife Management Area, the Aldrich Coal Mine Museum, the Heart of Dixie Railroad Museum, Shelby Iron Works Park and American Village among its places of interest.

Schools come from four public systems: Shelby County Schools, Alabaster City Schools, Pelham City Schools and Hoover City Schools. Private schools in the county include Briarwood Christian School and Indian Springs School. Which district a house falls into depends on the address, so check with the school systems rather than assuming.

A cash sale does not change the property tax steps. The buyer takes the house as is, taxes are settled at closing as the contract says, and the new owner reports the deed to the probate office.

faqs.q: When are Shelby County property taxes due?
faqs.a: October 1, and they become delinquent after December 31, according to the Alabama Department of Revenue. Unpaid taxes can go to a tax sale the following May.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay if I never got a tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes. The Revenue Department says counties are not required to mail notices and do so as a courtesy, so the tax is owed regardless.

faqs.q: What work on my Shelby County house has to be reported?
faqs.a: New structures, additions, pools, remodeling, added baths or fireplaces, patios, decks, carports and garages. Re-roofing, painting and minor repairs do not need a reassessment. The deadline is December 31 for work done on or before October 1.

faqs.q: Who pays the tax when a Shelby County house sells mid-year?
faqs.a: The state says the new owner answers for taxes on property they own, even if the bill carries the old owner's name. How the year is divided between buyer and seller is set in the sale contract.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Shelby County assessment?
faqs.a: We could not confirm the appeal process from an official Shelby County page, so ask the county tax office for the form and deadline.
